faq.q: Is it normal to feel lots of different feelings when someone dies?
faq.a: Yes. People who are grieving can feel sad, angry, scared, numb, guilty or even relieved, sometimes all in one day. There is no right or wrong way to grieve.
asks: Why do I feel angry after someone died?
Why do I feel nothing after someone died?

faq.a: It depends on the family and their culture or faith. Many hold a funeral or a gathering, say prayers or share stories, light candles, or visit a special place to remember.

faq.q: How can I remember someone who has died?
faq.a: You could make a memory box or a photo book, draw pictures, write them a letter, plant a flower, or cook their favourite food with your family.
asks: What can I do to remember my grandma?

faq.q: Is it okay to have fun when I am grieving?
faq.a: Yes. Playing and laughing is a healthy part of grieving, and it does not mean you have forgotten or stopped caring. Love and fun can live side by side.
asks: Is it wrong to laugh after someone died?

faq.q: Was it my fault that they died?
faq.a: No. Nothing you thought, said or did caused it. Lots of children worry about this, so if you do, tell a grown-up you trust, and they will help you understand what happened.

facts: Mexico's Day of the Dead, on 1 and 2 November, is a celebration where families remember loved ones who have died with photos, marigold flowers and their favourite foods.
Grief often comes in waves, with harder and calmer moments, and for most people it softens over time.
